newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says Michiquillay copper deposit sale delayed.
newsitem.headline: Peru says Michiquillay copper deposit sale delayed.

text.p: Peru's Minero Peru said late Monday it has postponed for up to two months the planned July 16 sale of its Michiquillay copper concession as bidders want legislation for tax breaks to reduce front-end investment.

"We have postponed the process for up to 60 days," said Oscar Arrieta, spokesman for the Michiquillay privatization board. "There are requests from the mining firms to see what the sales tax will be like."

The government has said it will pass legislation to help the cash-flow of companies developing mining projects by exempting them from paying levies on assets they buy during initial investment stages.

But Minero Peru, which was due to set a minimum bid price for Michiquillay last week, was forced to put off the sale -- originally planned for February -- because the proposed bill had not reached Congress, Arrieta said.

Minero Peru had selected seven U.S., Japanese and Canadian companies to bid for the exploration concession, whose reserves in the northern department of Cajamarca, have an average copper content of 0.7 percent. The mineral reserves also contain between 0.1 and 0.5 grams per tonne of gold and 0.5 to 5.0 grams per tonne of silver.
Minero Peru is the country's second state mining company after Centromin. Both companies are undergoing a piecemeal privatization process.
